items.headline: Baseball's best pitcher made his Dodgers debut — and got a Wrigley welcome
items.body: That blockbuster deadline trade got real Tuesday: two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal took the mound for the first time as a Dodger, at Wrigley Field, and struck out six over six innings. Cubs fans booed him every time he touched the ball — and Chicago actually beat him 5-1 — but a rotation with Skubal in it is a scary thing for the rest of the league come October.
items.say: The Dodgers finally pitched Skubal for the first time since that huge trade — Cubs fans booed him all night and actually beat him. Still, imagine that guy on the two-time champs. You catch any of it?

items.headline: The internet stopped for the 'Avengers: Doomsday' trailer — and 'Dunesday' is officially on
items.body: Marvel finally dropped the first full trailer for 'Avengers: Doomsday,' with Robert Downey Jr. back — this time as the villain, Doctor Doom — leading a stacked crossover of the Avengers, the Fantastic Four and the original X-Men. It opens December 18, the exact same day as 'Dune: Part Three,' so fans have already nicknamed the box-office clash 'Dunesday.' Big-budget nerd Christmas is coming.
items.say: Did you see the new Avengers: Doomsday trailer? Downey's back, but as the bad guy — and it opens the same day as the next Dune, so people are calling it 'Dunesday.' Which one are you seeing first?

items.headline: Leagues Cup is back — and Cincinnati put on a show against Pachuca
items.body: The MLS-vs-Liga MX summer tournament kicked off with six games, and FC Cincinnati stole opening night. After falling behind early, Brazilian playmaker Evander took over — a stunner from the edge of the box sparked a 3-1 comeback win over Liga MX side Pachuca in front of a rocking TQL Stadium. Across the border war's first night, MLS and Liga MX split the six openers 3-3.
items.say: The Leagues Cup started — it's basically the whole US league against the whole Mexican league, so every game's a grudge match. Cincinnati's Evander was unreal in a 3-1 win. You been catching any MLS?

items.headline: Believe again — 'Ted Lasso' is officially back today
items.body: After a three-year wait, 'Ted Lasso' Season 4 premieres today on Apple TV+, with Ted (Jason Sudeikis) taking on his biggest challenge yet: coaching a second-division women's team back in Richmond. The whole gang walked the red carpet in LA last night, and new episodes drop weekly through October. The feel-good comfort watch is back on the menu.
items.say: Ted Lasso's actually back today — first new season in three years, and this time he's coaching a women's team. If you loved the old ones it's a great week. You watch that show?

items.headline: The Red Sox are the hottest team in baseball — 24 of their last 27
items.body: Fenway is rocking: Boston hammered the White Sox 14-2 for a sixth straight win, fueled by Caleb Durbin's first career grand slam and a pair of homers from Wilyer Abreu. The Sox have now won 24 of their last 27 — the best stretch in the majors — and a team that looked ordinary in the spring suddenly looks like a real October threat.
items.say: The Red Sox are absolutely on fire — they've won like 24 of their last 27 and just put up 14 runs. Fun time to be a Boston fan. You follow baseball at all?

items.headline: Country's Ella Langley is rewriting the record books — 16 weeks at No. 1
items.body: If you've had a radio on this summer, you've heard it: Ella Langley's 'Choosin' Texas' just notched its 16th week atop the Billboard Hot 100, passing legends like Whitney Houston and Mariah Carey for the longest No. 1 run ever by a solo woman with a non-holiday song. A genuine country-pop phenomenon that refuses to leave the top spot.
items.say: That Ella Langley song 'Choosin' Texas' has been number one basically all summer — she just passed Whitney Houston and Mariah Carey for the longest run ever by a solo woman. Kind of wild. You heard it?

items.headline: The richest show in esports is happening right now — the Esports World Cup
items.body: If you know a gamer, they're glued to this: the Esports World Cup is running through August 23 in Paris, a giant multi-game festival where the top organizations battle across 20-plus titles for one of the biggest prize pools the scene has ever seen — a $27M club-championship pot alone, with $7M going to the winning org. Counter-Strike's championship headlines the grand finale later this month.
items.say: There's this giant esports festival on right now — the Esports World Cup — where all the big teams play a bunch of games for absurd prize money. The Counter-Strike final's the big one later this month. You into any of that?

items.headline: The last big US Open tune-up is on — and the draw blew wide open
items.body: The National Bank Open — a Masters 1000 for the men in Montreal and a WTA 1000 for the women in Toronto — is in full swing as the final hard-court runway to the US Open. With Sinner, Alcaraz and Djokovic all sitting this one out, the door is wide open: hometown favorite Félix Auger-Aliassime is the No. 2 seed carrying Canadian hopes, alongside stars like Alexander Zverev and Taylor Fritz. Great late-summer viewing.
items.say: The big Canadian tennis event's on — last tune-up before the US Open — and with the top three guys all skipping it, it's basically anyone's to grab. The local favorite's got the whole crowd behind him. You watch any tennis?

items.headline: Golden Gate Park turns into a festival — Outside Lands takes over this weekend
items.body: San Francisco's big summer blowout, Outside Lands, runs Friday through Sunday in Golden Gate Park with Charli XCX, The Strokes and Rufus Du Sol headlining, plus Turnstile, The xx, Death Cab for Cutie and a deep undercard. It's sold out, but Amazon Music is streaming sets live all weekend — fog, food trucks and a stacked lineup, no wristband required.
items.say: Outside Lands is this weekend in San Francisco — Charli XCX, The Strokes, the whole thing. It's sold out but they stream a bunch of it free. You ever done a festival like that?
